reviewed: Production release_held_token reads the stored owner and sends before removal. A failed send exits with the original token retained. Successful, absent or confirmed-dead releases remove only that token.
The same-target/VK union excludes the current token, preserving the prior first-release/no-UP and last-owner/UP semantics. Saved packet/window/source fields are retained for retry.

A vanished focused window release failure is handled within its user tick: keyboard recipient clears, held tokens and PID focus/lease remain pending; unrelated users continue. Existing process-exit handling later forgets the PID and removes dead native holds. Policy.release only clears that user root, so failure does not silently erase the selected PID lease.

The focused test invokes the exact production table transition with liveness/send closures. It proves another owner suppresses UP, the failed last-owner send retains its token, and successful retry emits the saved key-UP and removes ownership. No vendor/provider or product test hook.
